label: early original-phase steps (t=1-4) shortly after l/s/x/n/i/r/g/v
explanation: Fires only near the start of the sequence: steps t=1-4 of the original phase, plus the <DEL> step when it falls in that window (short L). Most of the activation mass (about 81%) is at t=2-4. It never fires at t=0, almost never at t>=6, and essentially never during the copy phase. Within that window it depends on which tokens came just before: the rate is about 3.5x higher when the previous token (or the one two back) is one of l, s, x, n, i, and somewhat higher for r, g, v. The largest activations (about 1.0 of max) are at <DEL> after short sequences like q l s <DEL> or 3 l l <DEL>, i.e. when l/s/x have just been seen. Repeated tokens (in_first=0) rarely activate it. The predicate (t in 1-4, phase<=1, prev or prev2 token in {l,s,x,n,i,r,g,v}) gets dev P=0.71, R=0.86, F1=0.77, mass recall 0.92. The leftover misses are weak activations after other tokens, and the false positives are in-window steps where the feature stays silent despite a matching preceding token, so the token dependence is graded rather than a strict set.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the previous input (most: l, s, x, n, i, r; least: k, 0, u, j) and the input two steps back (most: l, s, x, n, v, i; least: t, u, 0, j); timing cues that raise it most: t=3, t=2, t=4.
